title: {Il faut que...} - Saying What's Necessary
description: Learn to tell people what needs to happen! Essential phrases for parents, friends, work. '{Il faut que tu manges}' (You need to eat), '{Il faut qu'on parte}' (We need to leave).
can_do: Express necessity and requirements (It's necessary that...)
Tell people what needs to happen
Use '{il faut que}' with subjunctive forms naturally

vocabulary.fr: il faut que tu sois sage
il faut que tu fasses attention

concepts.definition: Tell SOMEONE SPECIFIC what needs to happen. More direct than 'il faut + verb'
concepts.example: {Il faut manger} (general: someone should eat) → {Il faut que tu manges} (YOU specifically need to eat); {Il faut qu'on aille au parc} (We need to go to the park)

concepts.definition: These phrases are used constantly in daily life!
concepts.example: Parent to kid: '{Il faut que tu finisses tes devoirs}' (You need to finish homework)

items.situation: Tell your kid they need to eat (lunch is ready!)

mistakes.feedback: That's general! To tell SOMEONE specific, use: il faut que tu manges

items.situation: Tell your friend they need to leave now
Tell your group 'I need to go' (have to leave early)

mistakes.feedback: Use '{aille}' not 'vais' after il faut que: j'aille

items.situation: Tell your friends 'we need to leave' (time to go!)
Tell a child they need to be good (parent language!)
items.answer: il faut que tu sois sage

mistakes.answer: il faut que tu es sage
mistakes.feedback: Use '{sois}' not 'es' after il faut que: tu sois sage

items.situation: Tell someone they need to pay attention (be careful!)
items.answer: il faut que tu fasses attention

items.situation: Say 'she needs to come' (expecting someone to arrive)

mistakes.feedback: Use '{vienne}' not 'vient' after il faut que: elle vienne
